## Osthoff's posting to Turkey is cancelled

**Sources on this page:** p149 A2. [Concise case study](../people/osthoff.md).

**Shared edition.** The following reading also discusses [p138 A1](138.md#source-p138-a1), [p138 A2](138.md#source-p138-a2), [p148 C1](148.md#source-p148-c1).

<a id="edition-cases-people-osthoff-osthoffs-posting-to-turkey-is-cancelled"></a>


[ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [All readings](../README.md) · [Source audit](../../experiments/corpus_attack/SOURCE_FAMILIES.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

Four receptions, p138 A1–A2 and p148 C1 / p149 A2, reconstruct the cancellation of Osthoff's posting to Turkey. Under the published **Nov4–6** key, they jointly support all **121 positions** of the first part and **115 of 118** in the second; three word repairs complete the proposed reading.

<a id="edition-cases-people-osthoff-most-likely-reading"></a>

### Most likely reading

**Readable German:**

> Militärmission Konstantinopel. Kommando des Hptms. der Res. Osthoff nach der Türkei und seine Zuteilung zur Militärmission ist aufgehoben. Derselbe ist dem 1. Ers. Batl. Eisenbahn-Regmts. zu überweisen. AKO folgt. Auf Allerhöchsten Befehl: Chef Militärkabinetts, Frhr. Marschall.

**English meaning:** To the Military Mission in Constantinople. Captain of the Reserve Osthoff's posting to Turkey and assignment to the Military Mission have been cancelled. He is to be transferred to the first replacement battalion of the railway regiment. The cabinet order will follow. By supreme command: the Chief of the Military Cabinet, Baron Marschall.

The English expands the military abbreviations *Ers. Batl.* and *AKO*. The cancellation concerns Osthoff's assignment. His full identity and the regiment number remain unestablished.

<a id="edition-cases-people-osthoff-what-the-witnesses-establish"></a>

### What the witnesses establish

| Part | Printed witnesses | Direct source evidence | Remaining editorial work |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [p138 A1](../../experiments/corpus_attack/sources/childs_p138_A.png), [p148 C1](../../experiments/corpus_attack/sources/childs_p148_C1.png) | p148 fixes 120/121 positions. The other witness supplies the missing `R` in `DERRES`. All 121 candidate positions have complete coordinate-pair support in a witness. | The earlier p138 copy is five coordinates short. A unique best alignment among all 238 insertion positions supplies `XVAXX` before received index 140. Three other known-coordinate disagreements remain. |
| 2 | [p138 A2](../../experiments/corpus_attack/sources/childs_p138_A.png), [p149 A2](../../experiments/corpus_attack/sources/childs_p149_A2.png) | The two copies jointly support 115/118 proposed positions. p149 independently supplies the `N` in `KABINETTS` and the `C` in `HOECHSTEN`. | Both copies contain `UEM`, `ERSBKTL` and `REGM1S`. Reading `DEM`, `ERSBATL` and `REGMTS` requires three changes in p149 and four in the more damaged p138 copy. |

The literal p149 second part is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
DERSELBEISTUEM1XERSBKTLEISENBAHNREGM1SZUUEBERWEISENAKOFOLGTXAUFALLERHOECHSTENBEFEHLCHEFMILITAERKABINETTSFRHRMARSCHALLX
```

</details>

Two repairs form the adjacent coordinate exchange `VF → FV` at transmitted indices 210–211; the third changes index 31 from `A` to `X`. The [certificate](../../experiments/corpus_attack/source_pair_results.json) records the raw readings, source differences, coordinate maps and repair costs.

<a id="edition-cases-people-osthoff-dates-and-provenance"></a>

### Dates and provenance

The p138 header gives 5 November; the clearer p148–149 transmission was intercepted on 7 November and includes `0015 (6/11)`. Both parts use the unchanged published **Nov4–6** key. The later interception time therefore does not by itself require a new period key.

The historical records are from J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*, printed pp. 138, 148–149 in the [source scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view). The period-key work is credited to **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker**, with the public key also given by George Lasry in the [2017 discussion](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1).

Source comparison, reconstruction and edition: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

## Kremp's request for a departure date — p131, p149 and p159

**Sources on this page:** p149 B. [Concise case study](../people/kremp.md).

**Shared edition.** The following reading also discusses [p131 B](131.md#source-p131-b), [p159 D](159.md#source-p159-d).

<a id="edition-cases-people-kremp-kremps-request-for-a-departure-date--p131-p149-and-p159"></a>



Kremp reports his recovery and asks the military mission's transport section to set his departure date. The unlettered final message on p159 reads completely under the published **Nov7–9** key: **98 positions, with no source correction**. Its different-key reception also repairs the earlier p131 B / p149 B version.

<a id="edition-cases-people-kremp-reading"></a>

### Reading

**Readable German:**

> Coeln 11. Ab. 1. S. Milmiss., Transp.-Abt. 1b, Constantinopel.
> Bin wiederhergestellt. Bitte Abfahrtstag bestimmen. Kremp.

**Meaning:** Kremp reports that he has recovered and asks the transport section
of the military mission in Constantinople to specify his departure date.
The opening `COELN11XAB1XSX` is directly decoded; its administrative meaning remains unknown. The displayed spacing and abbreviation breaks are editorial.

The complete p159 plaintext is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
COELN11XAB1XSXMILMISSTRANSPABT1BCONSTANTINOPELXBINWIEDERHERGESTELLTBITTEABFAHRTSTAGBESTIMMENXKREMP
```

</details>

All 196 source coordinates re-encrypt exactly using established square cells.

<a id="edition-cases-people-kremp-three-source-witnesses"></a>

### Three source witnesses

| Witness | Source heading and receipt | Key | Directly fixed positions |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| [p131 B](../../experiments/open_targets_continuation/sources/childs_p131_selected.png) | 5 November, continued; received 6 November at 02:36 | `Nov4-6` | 82/84 |
| [p149 B](../../experiments/open_targets_continuation/sources/childs_p149_selected.png) | 6 November, continued; received 7 November at 08:59; internal `0110 (6/11)` | `Nov4-6` | 84/84 |
| [p159, final unlettered item](../../experiments/open_targets_continuation/sources/childs_p159_selected.png) | 9 November; received at 06:12; internal `NR 17 (9/11)` | `Nov7-9` | 98/98 |

The last item follows a fresh **9 November** heading below the three messages
under 8 November. The machine-readable identifier `p159_D` is a local label
for the fourth item; the source itself does not print a `D` beside it.

The p131 and p149 ciphertexts differ at three slots: two p131 dashes correspond to p149 `A`s, and one `D` corresponds to `V`. The p159 reception uses a different transposition, square and address prefix. Its 51-character body matches **48 of 51** directly decoded characters in p149 and **45 of 51** in p131.

<a id="edition-cases-people-kremp-exact-repairs-to-the-earlier-version"></a>

### Exact repairs to the earlier version

The p149 source decodes literally as:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
MILMISTRANSPABT1BKONSTANTINOPELXBINWIEDERHER4ESTELLTBITTEABFA7ETSTAGBESTIMMENXKREMPX
```

</details>

The independently readable p159 body supports `WIEDERHERGESTELLT` and
`ABFAHRTSTAG`. The resulting p149 reconstruction requires precisely three
changes to valid source coordinates, with no insertions or erasure fills:

| Source index, zero based | Printed | Proposed | Plaintext effect |
| ---: | :---: | :---: | --- |
| 134 | X | V | `4` becomes `G` in `WIEDERHERGESTELLT`. |
| 26 | D | G | `7` becomes `H` in `ABFAHRTSTAG`. |
| 106 | F | V | The following `E` becomes `R`. |

The remaining **165 printed coordinates** and the earlier address forms `MILMIS` and `KONSTANTINOPEL` are retained. The 84-position reconstruction re-encrypts to this three-change witness.

For p131, the same body additionally fills its two dashes and changes source
index 145 from `D` to `V`, yielding `BITTE` followed by `ABFAHRTSTAG`.
Its complete repair cost is **four known-coordinate substitutions and two erasure fills**.

## An enquiry about Glatz's whereabouts

**Sources on this page:** p149 C. [Concise case study](../people/glatz.md).

**Shared edition.** The following reading also discusses [p140 B](140.md#source-p140-b).

<a id="edition-cases-people-glatz-an-enquiry-about-glatzs-whereabouts"></a>


[ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [All readings](../README.md) · [Source audit](../../experiments/corpus_attack/SOURCE_FAMILIES.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Records:** p140 B and p149 C. **Result:** 167 of 168 proposed positions have complete coordinate-pair support in a printed witness under the published Nov4–6 key. One damaged glyph needs an explicit reading to complete `KONSTANTINOPEL`.

<a id="edition-cases-people-glatz-most-likely-reading"></a>

### Most likely reading

**Readable German:**

> Militär-Mission Konstantinopel. Drahtnachricht über Verbleib Reg. Bmstr. Glatz vom Straßenbau-Sonderkommando 1 erbeteten [wohl: erbeten]. Milverkehr, röm. 2 A 100166 Ko, durch Admiralstab, Kz. 95537.

**Display notes:** The bracketed `[wohl: erbeten]` is a proposed ordinary-German normalization of the literal `ERBETETEN`. It is a gloss, not a deletion in either exact output. Abbreviation expansions in the meaning below remain interpretations; the following notes distinguish the uncertain institutional terms.

The literal numeral label after `ROEM` remains `2` in the readable version;
it is not replaced by a Roman-numeral rendering.

**English meaning:** To the Military Mission in Constantinople. A telegram is requested reporting the whereabouts of Government Master Builder Glatz of Road Construction Special Detachment 1. The closing contains routing and reference information, including transmission through the Admiral Staff and reference 95537.

*Reg. Bmstr.* is probably *Regierungsbaumeister*. The precise institutional meanings of `MILVERKEHR`, `ROEM 2 A 100166 KO` and `KZ 95537` are not established here. The source-supported wording is **ERBETETEN**, with an extra `TE` compared with ordinary **ERBETEN**. The readable edition marks this irregularity; the fixed-length candidate retains all its letters.

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
MILITAERXMISSIONKONSTANTINOPELXDRAHTNACHRICHTUEBERVERBLEIBREGXBMSTRXGLATZVOMSTRASSENBAUSONDERKOMMANDO1ERBETETENXMILVERKEHRXROEMX2XAX100166XKOXDURCHADMIRALSTABXKZX95537X
```

</details>

<a id="edition-cases-people-glatz-source-support-and-remaining-repair"></a>

### Source support and remaining repair

Both printed copies contain 336 coordinate slots. In [p140 B](../../experiments/corpus_attack/sources/childs_p140_B.png), the last character of group 64, `VDAF?`, is visibly damaged. All other **335 legible coordinates** directly yield the candidate above. Supplying `X` at this source slot (index 319) gives pair `VX` = `I` at plaintext position 24, completing `KONSTANTINOPEL`. This is the explicit editorial fill; the damaged glyph remains masked in the source transcription.

The [p149 C](../../experiments/corpus_attack/sources/childs_p149_C.png) copy has a clear final `G` in that group. It gives `VG` = `B`, hence `KONSTANTBNOPEL`; it does not independently supply the proposed `I`. Three other coordinate disagreements produce `STRKSSENBAU`, `ERBETETRN` and `4ILVERKEHR`. The proposed candidate costs zero known-coordinate substitutions in p140 and four in p149, plus the one p140 damaged-glyph fill. It is not the absolute minimum-disagreement candidate: retaining `KONSTANTBNOPEL` would lower the combined cost from four to three. The preference for the normal place-name is therefore explicit editorial reasoning.

The [certificate](../../experiments/corpus_attack/source_pair_results.json) records both raw texts, the four substitutions and the source coordinates supporting every proposed letter. The [source inputs](../../experiments/corpus_attack/source_pairs.json) preserve the literal transcriptions and complete headers.

<a id="edition-cases-people-glatz-dates-and-provenance"></a>

### Dates and provenance

Both headers give **6 November 1918**: 4.00 p.m. in p140 and 7.54 p.m. in p149. The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*, printed pp. 140 and 149 in the [complete scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).

The unchanged **Nov4–6** period key retains the credit recorded in [data/keys.json](../../data/keys.json): **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker**, with the public key also supplied by George Lasry in the [2017 discussion](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1). Source comparison, reconstruction, repair analysis and this edition are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. No first historical decipherment priority is claimed.
